articles.topic: Brain training improves cognition task performance
articles.headline: Brain Training Beats Comparison Groups on Cognitive Tasks
articles.body: A large randomized trial called BRIGHT-Mind tested Lumosity, a digital brain-training program, in healthy adults and found it significantly improved overall cognition compared to a control group. Participants reported real-world functional improvements in work, school, and home life. Even more striking: brain scans showed structural changes in older adults after just 12 weeks. The improvements appeared on measures of cognition-related disability that most behavioral interventions don't typically produce measurable brain changes for.
articles.takeaway: If cognitive performance matters to you, accessible at-home training might actually work. The brain responds to practiced challenge in measurable ways.

articles.topic: Hormone therapy protects menopausal bone density
articles.headline: Menopausal Hormone Therapy Cuts Low Bone Density Risk by 69%
articles.body: New data from ENDO 2026 shows menopausal hormone therapy significantly reduces the risk of low bone mineral density. Among 387 postmenopausal women, those taking hormone therapy had 69% lower odds of osteopenia or osteoporosis at the spine and hip, even after accounting for age, vitamin D, and other health factors. The benefit holds real value for women early after menopause, offering more than symptom relief. This real-world evidence supports what clinicians have known but underutilized: hormones protect skeletal health alongside managing hot flashes.
articles.takeaway: If you're early in menopause, hormone therapy might protect your bones as much as it helps your symptoms. Talk to your doctor about timing and your individual risk.
articles.source: Medical News Today, via Endocrine Society (June 2026)

articles.headline: Sugar-Free Electrolyte Drinks Rehydrate Better Than Plain Water
articles.body: A new study from Arizona State University tested a novel sugar-free electrolyte formula combining allulose, amino acids, and electrolytes against plain water and traditional sports drinks. The sugar-free formula retained 46.6% of fluid at 4 hours post-exercise compared to 24.8% for water alone. Body weight was significantly better restored with the sugar-free version. The twist: you don't need added sugar to absorb fluid effectively. For busy parents doing noon workouts or evening training, this means you can hydrate smarter without the carb load.
articles.takeaway: If you need hydration without fuel, sugar-free electrolyte formulas work. Plain water falls short when sweat losses are real.

articles.topic: DNA methylation clocks reveal biological aging rates
articles.headline: Your DNA Methylation Pattern Predicts How Fast You're Aging
articles.body: New meta-analysis of over 15,000 DNA methylation profiles across 17 human tissues shows aging produces both conserved patterns and tissue-specific signatures. As you age, specific sites in your DNA accumulate methylation changes in predictable ways. These epigenetic clocks—like GrimAge and DunedinPACE—now reliably predict health outcomes and mortality better than chronological age alone. The pattern also reveals which tissues are aging fastest in you personally. This isn't science fiction anymore. Your blood can reveal whether your body is aging like a 50-year-old at 45 or staying young longer.
articles.takeaway: DNA methylation clocks reveal your true biological age. Smoking cessation and healthy behaviors can measurably slow the clock.

workout.title: Threshold Tempo Ladder: Progressive Race-Pace Sustainability
workout.tip: Use perceived exertion to dial in pace rather than obsessing over GPS. During tempo blocks, you should be able to speak only short phrases (4–5 words max). If you can sing, you're too easy; if you can't speak at all, you're too hard.
workout.warmup: 10 min easy Z2 jog, 5×20 sec buildout strides (accelerate each stride) with 90 sec recovery jog between each

exercises.name: Easy Aerobic Primer
exercises.notes: Z2 conversational pace, HR 60–70% max. Establish smooth cadence (170–180 rpm), relax shoulders, feel your rhythm.

exercises.name: Tempo Ladder Block 1
exercises.notes: Tempo/threshold pace (Z4, HR 85–88% max). This is your half-marathon goal pace or just below marathon goal pace. Stay controlled and smooth.

exercises.name: Recovery Jog
exercises.notes: Easy Z2. HR drops 10–15 bpm. Mental reset. Optional light fueling: 25–50 cal carbs if needed.

exercises.name: Tempo Ladder Block 2
exercises.notes: Maintain Z4 tempo pace (85–88% HR max). The ladder lengthens effort duration—your mind must settle into the discomfort. Focus on relaxed arms and steady breathing.

exercises.name: Recovery Jog
exercises.notes: Easy Z2. Let HR recover fully. Consume 50 cal carbs if available. Prepare mentally for the final, longest block.

exercises.name: Tempo Ladder Block 3 (Peak Effort)
exercises.notes: Sustain Z4 tempo pace (85–88% HR max). This is the mental crescendo—the longest tempo block. Legs will feel heavy; this is the adaptation stimulus. Breathe deeply, hold form.

exercises.name: Cool-Down Easy Jog
exercises.notes: Z2 easy pace. Gradually bring HR down. Celebrate pushing through sustained effort.

workout.cooldown: 5 min walking, then: standing quad stretch 40 sec each leg, hamstring fold 60 sec, glute figure-4 45 sec each side, calf stretch 30 sec each leg. Refuel with 20–30g protein + 40–60g carbs within 30 min of completion.
workout.description: A 75-minute structured long run using a ladder format to build lactate threshold and race-pace endurance without excessive fatigue. Athletes warm into three progressive tempo efforts (7, 9, and 11 minutes) at half-marathon or marathon goal pace with brief recovery jogs between, developing mental toughness and pacing consistency under fatigue. Perfect for intermediate marathon and Olympic-distance triathlon athletes building aerobic power and race-specific speed.

meal.title: Chicken & Veggie Naan Pizza
meal.description: A fast flatbread pizza on naan with chicken, peppers, spinach and melty mozzarella.
ingredients: ¼ cup marinara or pizza sauce
3 oz cooked chicken breast (rotisserie is fine), chopped
meal.instructions: 1. Heat the oven to 425°F. 2. Spread the sauce on the naan and top with the spinach, chicken, peppers and mozzarella. 3. Bake directly on the rack 8–10 minutes until the cheese bubbles.
